question: How often can changing one bit flip a polynomial threshold decision?
idea: Evaluate a polynomial on a string of bits, then report only whether its value is nonnegative. The manuscript claims the average number of individual bits that can change that decision is at most eight times the polynomial’s degree times the square root of the number of bits.

exactClaim: Proves that a degree-at-most-d polynomial threshold function on the uniform n-dimensional Boolean cube has average sensitivity at most $8d\sqrt n$, uniformly for $1\le d\le n$. Average sensitivity counts expected output changes under single-bit flips. This establishes the asymptotic Gotsman–Linial conjecture, allowing polynomial zeros with $\mathop{\mathrm{sign}}\nolimits (0)=1$. )
